themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 17 this week versus a baseline average of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 807% surge (z-score: 9.85)—suggesting a possible public health or sanitation breakdown in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights that demands immediate investigation.
evidence: 17 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (807% increase)
Z-score of 9.85 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing aligns with winter season (animal die-off risk) but magnitude is unprecedented in 8-week record
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Sanitation Department about response protocols and whether they've identified a source (contamination, disease, structural hazard)
Canvass affected blocks to document locations and get resident accounts of what they've observed

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, up 967% from a baseline of 0.4 per week, and separately 13 complaints hit 2 weeks ago (up 197% from baseline)—a sustained spike suggesting widespread electrical infrastructure strain or safety issues.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
13 electrical complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.4 weekly baseline (197% spike, z-score: 5.77)
Combined z-scores and recency indicate acute, ongoing infrastructure event
reporting_angles: Request Con Edison outage logs and planned maintenance schedules for Bay Ridge to check for grid stress or aging infrastructure
File FOIL request with DOB for electrical violation notices filed in the past 2 weeks in the district

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints more than tripled to 34 last week versus an 11.0 per week baseline over 8 weeks—a 209% surge (z-score: 7.1)—indicating either new construction/commercial activity or quality-of-life degradation worth documenting.
evidence: 34 noise complaints last week vs. 11.0 weekly baseline (209% increase, z-score: 7.1)
Two active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (9201 4th Ave, 9818 Fort Hamilton Parkway) may correlate with construction noise
439 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, with 370 alterations—construction activity spike could explain noise surge
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaint locations with active DOB permit sites and ULURP projects
Interview residents on affected blocks to understand source (construction, traffic, nightlife, other) and impact on sleep/health

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Activity
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints hit 9 two weeks ago, a 929% spike from a baseline of 0.9 per week (z-score: 7.71)—coinciding with late-winter/early-spring period and potentially signaling organized or gang-related activity worth monitoring.
evidence: 9 illegal fireworks complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (929% spike, z-score: 7.71)
Spike is sustained and statistically extreme, not a one-off anomaly
No Reddit or community board data yet, suggesting residents may not yet be escalating complaints beyond 311
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD 62nd Precinct about enforcement activity and whether they've identified hotspots or organized activity
Map 311 complaints geographically to identify which blocks are epicenters and what's nearby (vacant lots, parks, gathering spots)

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Anomaly (Decline)
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 53% to 182 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 389.8 per week (z-score: -7.66)—a counterintuitive decline that may reflect either improved enforcement, resident disengagement from 311, or data processing delays worth investigating.
evidence: 182 illegal parking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 389.8 weekly baseline (53% decrease, z-score: -7.66)
Decline is statistically significant and recent, not gradual trend
Contradicts typical winter pattern (snow/ice should increase illegal parking complaints)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD Traffic Enforcement to confirm if they launched new parking enforcement initiative this week
Verify with 311 that complaint processing is functioning normally and no data backlog exists
